science.title: Rezvilutamide versus bicalutamide with androgen-deprivation therapy in high-volume metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer: a multicenter retrospective cohort study
science.description: Real-world comparison of rezvilutamide versus bicalutamide in high-volume metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) is limited. While the phase III CHART trial established the efficacy of rezvilutamide in a controlled setting, its generalizability to routine clinical practice, particularly in patients excluded from the trial (e.g., those with prior docetaxel exposure), remains uncertain. Multicenter retrospective cohort study of high-volume mHSPC patients receiving ADT plus rezvilutamide or bicalutamide (2021–2024). Propensity-score matching (1:1) yielded 50 patients per group. Calendar year was not included in the primary propensity-score model but was incorporated as a covariate in prespecified sensitivity analyses to address potential treatment-era bias. Primary endpoint: radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS). Rezvilutamide significantly improved median rPFS (25.9 vs. 16.1 months; HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.41–0.98; p = 0.038), time to castration resistance (18.6 vs. 11.4 months; HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.39–0.94; p = 0.026), and time to PSA progression (20.1 vs. 12.9 months; HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.36–0.91; p = 0.018). PSA50 (84% vs. 62%; p = 0.011) and PSA90 (50% vs. 28%; p = 0.022) responses favored rezvilutamide. Overall survival (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.50–1.43; p = 0.54) and symptomatic skeletal events (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.44–1.54; p = 0.53) showed numerical benefit without significance. In exploratory analyses of patients with prior docetaxel exposure (24% of each group)—a population excluded from CHART—the rPFS point estimate favored rezvilutamide (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.30–1.55), though underpowered. Grade ≥ 3 adverse events were comparable (26% vs. 24%). Prespecified CNS-related events, defined using standardized criteria with independent neurologist review, were lower with rezvilutamide (8% vs. 14%). Rezvilutamide plus ADT provides superior disease control to bicalutamide plus ADT in high-volume mHSPC with a favorable safety profile. These real-world findings complement the CHART trial by including populations excluded from the trial, though the modest sample size limits definitive conclusions for subgroups. Longer-term follow-up is needed to confirm survival benefits.

science.title: Independently modulated genes in Streptococcus pneumoniae TIGR4 reveal transcriptional rewiring in antibiotic-adapted and antibiotic-sensitive strains
science.description: Streptococcus pneumoniae remains a major pathogen, and increasing antimicrobial resistance complicates disease control. To investigate transcriptional programs associated with antibiotic stress and adaptation, we applied independent component analysis (ICA) to a compendium of 718 RNA-seq datasets from the TIGR4 strain. ICA identified 60 independently modulated gene sets (iModulons), 30 of which significantly overlapped with known regulons. iModulon activity profiles distinguished adaptation-associated and antibiotic-induced transcriptional responses across multiple antibiotic conditions. The CiaRH iModulon recapitulated key features of the known CiaRH regulon despite the absence of ciaR/H mutant transcriptomes. Vancomycin-responsive activation of the CiaRH iModulon was observed in both TIGR4 and serotype 19F strains in nutrient-rich medium and independently reproduced in TIGR4 cultured under chemically defined conditions. However, most iModulon responses differed between TIGR4 and serotype 19F, suggesting these findings may not generalize across pneumococcal strains. These findings demonstrate that iModulon analysis provides a scalable and interpretable framework for characterizing transcriptional rewiring associated with antibiotic stress and adaptation in S. pneumoniae TIGR4. iModulon analysis is applied to Streptococcus pneumoniae TIGR4 RNA-seq data. Independently modulated genes reveal transcriptional rewiring in antibiotic-adapted and antibiotic-sensitive strains, providing a scalable, interpretable framework.

science.title: DARE to wear: digital health promotion and disease prevention using wearable devices
science.description: Global healthcare systems are under increasing strain to ensure long-term sustainability, necessitating a transition towards proactive, preventive healthcare strategies. Wearable sensor technologies are uniquely positioned to facilitate this paradigm shift by allowing continuous physiological and behavioral monitoring, facilitating early risk stratification, and enabling timely interventions. DigitAl lifelong pREvention (DARE) is a nationwide initiative conceived in Italy to develop and evaluate novel digital tools and services aimed at fostering innovative health promotion and disease prevention pathways, with wearable devices identified as a critical enabling technology. Herein, we present a comprehensive overview of 16 investigations designed in DARE to assess the utility of wearable devices in the continuous monitoring of physical activity, joint mobility, sleep, heart rate variability, nutrition, and glucose homeostasis across diverse health domains, including healthy aging, chronic disease prevention, and lifestyle modification programs targeting over 8000 participants. We meticulously detail the methodological characteristics of these study protocols, explicitly outlining the technical specifications, functional capabilities, and inherent limitations of 18 distinct wearable devices (sourced from 12 manufacturers) employed across these trials. The breadth of applications and the heterogeneity of the target populations underscore the significant potential of wearable devices as an integral component of future digital health prevention strategies.

science.title: Understanding and supporting university students’ use of distributed practice via implementation intentions
science.description: Effective learning strategies like distributed practice are essential for lifelong learning, yet students struggle to apply them consistently due to habitually using ineffective strategies and poor time-management. Setting goals of when and how to incorporate effective strategies could help bridge the gap between intention and behavior. We tested a goal-directed planning intervention using implementation intentions to support students in integrating distributed practice within their self-regulated learning and examined how self-regulated learning unfolds within students’ authentic context. We tracked daily study behavior of 87 university students (k = 1623) via experience sampling over a four-week course. Implementation intentions did not increase use of distributed practice. However, students who formulated implementation intentions reported shorter study durations, lower effort, and greater concentration during exam week, suggesting more efficient studying. Regardless of the intervention, students adapted to exam proximity by studying longer, reporting higher effort, satisfaction, extrinsic motivation, and more retrieval-based learning strategies. These findings provide longitudinal insights into how students regulate their learning over time and highlight assessment as a key driver of study behavior.

science.title: Surveillance of Mytella strigata using eDNA and local ecological knowledge: implications for management and alternative feed use
science.description: The brackish-water mussel Mytella strigata, native to Central and South America, has recently spread to Asian waters, raising concerns for aquaculture and biodiversity. This study presents a regional assessment along India’s southwest coast, integrating local ecological knowledge (LEK), environmental DNA (eDNA) monitoring, and nutritional analysis. Interviews and surveys with fisherfolk in Kerala revealed the species' rapid spread and associated issues, including clogging aquaculture cages, disrupting green mussel and oyster farms, and competing with native clams and mussels. By contrast, fishers in Goa reported no awareness or sightings of the mussel. Molecular evidence corroborated these findings: eDNA tests confirmed Mytella strigata's presence in Kerala's estuaries, while no detection was recorded in Goa during the survey. Nutritional profiling showed low protein, high erucic acid, and limited polyunsaturated fats, suggesting poor value for human consumption but potential as an affordable feed ingredient for poultry and aquaculture. Overall, the findings confirm the invasion of Mytella strigata in Kerala, underscore its ecological and economic impacts, and demonstrate the importance of combining fisherfolk insights with molecular tools. The study highlights the need for regular eDNA surveillance, active fisherfolk engagement, and policy actions to prevent further spread and protect India’s coastal biodiversity and aquaculture sectors.
